description: THE DUAL-TRUNCATION AND ACCUMULATION CASE. It does three jobs at once, and the three are separable so a failure localises. It lands TWO independent truncating divisions whose RoundingMode.DOWN results differ from what a half-rounding mode would give; it proves ADD WS-MONTHLY-INT TO WS-TOTAL-INT at app/cbl/CBACT04C.cbl:467 accumulates across rows WITHIN one account; and it proves WS-TRANID-SUFFIX advances once per WRITE rather than once per account. Two TCATBALF rows, ONE account, two distinct transaction-category keys - which is the smallest input that can make all three statements at the same time. THE ARITHMETIC, BOTH SITES. COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200 at :464-465 carries no ROUNDED phrase - the keyword appears zero times across all 28 programs - so the receiver WS-MONTHLY-INT PIC S9(09)V99 at :168 truncates on store, which in Java is setScale(2, RoundingMode.DOWN) through common.CobolDecimal, whose MONETARY_SCALE is 2 and whose COBOL_ROUNDING is the only mode it will apply. Row 1: 147.00 at 15.00 gives the exact product 2205.0000 and the exact quotient 1.8375, whose third decimal digit is seven, so DOWN gives 1.83 while BOTH HALF_UP and HALF_EVEN give 1.84 - a three-way discriminator. Row 2: 194.00 at 15.00 gives 2910.0000 and the exact quotient 2.4250, sitting exactly on the halfway boundary, so DOWN gives 2.42 and HALF_UP gives 2.43; HALF_EVEN also gives 2.42 here because the retained digit is even, which is precisely why row 1 is in the case as well. Between them the two rows exclude every excluded mode at least once. TRAN-AMT is therefore 0000000018C and 0000000024B, eleven zoned bytes each for S9(09)V99 with the sign overpunched into the LOW-ORDER byte under the positive table {ABCDEFGHI, so the digit strings are 00000000183 and 00000000242 and the trailing 3 and 2 become C and B. A run reporting 0000000018D or 0000000024C has rounded where the COBOL truncated. THE ACCUMULATION, AND A CORRECTION TO THE CASE BRIEF THAT MAKES THIS CASE SHARPER THAN THE BRIEF CLAIMED. :467 adds each truncated monthly figure into WS-TOTAL-INT, so after two rows WS-TOTAL-INT holds 1.83 + 2.42 = 4.25. The brief states that truncating per row and then summing, versus summing the exact quotients and truncating once at the end, would give the same answer here. They do NOT. 1.8375 + 2.4250 = 4.2625, which truncates once to 4.26 - a cent MORE than 4.25. So the ordering is directly discriminated by these operands rather than merely illustrated by them, and the discrimination is visible in the two written amounts: each was truncated BEFORE the add, so they sum to 4.25, whereas an implementation that deferred truncation to the accumulator would have written amounts summing to 4.2625. This is documented rather than absorbed, because a case whose stated reasoning is weaker than its actual evidence invites the next reader to relax it. WHERE THE 4.25 LIVES, AND WHY NO ACCOUNT ROW IS REWRITTEN. It does not reach ACCT-CURR-BAL in this run, and the zero-rewrite expectation below is a positive assertion rather than an omission. Both seeded rows belong to account 00000000001, so TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM at :194 is TRUE for row 1 and FALSE for row 2 - WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM is PIC X(11) VALUE SPACES at :167, so the comparison is alphanumeric against the account id's eleven-digit display image, and :201 has already stored 00000000001 into it by the time row 2 is read. There is therefore exactly ONE account break and it is the FIRST: WS-FIRST-TIME is still Y at :195, so :198 merely flips the flag and 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT does not run. Its only other call site, the ELSE at :219-220, is unreachable dead code - the enclosing PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' at :188 makes the IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' at :189 always true - so the final account group's accumulated interest is never flushed, and here the only account IS the last one. The 4.25 is proved indirectly, by the two independently truncated amounts on SYSTRAN. The DIRECT observation of WS-TOTAL-INT reaching ACCT-CURR-BAL belongs to case11.json, which needs a second account to force a non-first break; see that case for the rewrite itself. Preserving this defect rather than repairing it is practice B5: a job that rewrote the last group would be a new feature and a parity violation. THE SUFFIX SEQUENCE IS A FIRST-CLASS ASSERTION. ADD 1 TO WS-TRANID-SUFFIX at :474 sits inside 1300-B-WRITE-TX, which :468 performs once per WRITE and not once per account, so the suffixes are 000001 then 000002 even though both records belong to one account. A single record carrying suffix 000001 would mean the implementation writes per account; two records both carrying 000001 would mean the counter was hoisted out of the write. And because WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is PIC 9(06) VALUE 0 at :173 and the ADD precedes the STRING at :476-480, the sequence starts at 1 and never at 000000. PARM-DATE contributes the ten characters of app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:22 PARM='2022071800' verbatim, never parsed as a date, so 10 + 6 fills TRAN-ID PIC X(16) exactly with no padding. THE RATE LOOKUP RUNS PER RECORD, NOT PER ACCOUNT, AND THAT IS WHY THE FALLBACK PAIR APPEARS TWICE. :210-213 move ACCT-GROUP-ID, TRANCAT-CD and TRANCAT-TYPE-CD into the disclosure-group key and perform 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE at the same nesting level as the account-break IF, that is OUTSIDE it, so the READ at :416 happens on every iteration. Both records therefore take the :422 tolerated '23' path and both display :418 DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING and :419 TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE, giving eight lines in total: the start line, three for row 1, three for row 2, and the end line. An implementation that hoisted the rate lookup into the break handler would produce six lines and still compute the right amounts, which is exactly the kind of ordering error a byte-comparison of amounts alone cannot see. WHY BOTH READS MISS, VERIFIED MECHANICALLY, AND A CORRECTION TO THE FOLDER BRIEF. The folder brief claims acctdata's A000000000 is a group id that steers account rows into the DISCGRP A-block. It is not. Read against app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, A000000000 sits in ACCT-ADDR-ZIP at 1-based 103-112 while ACCT-GROUP-ID at 113-122 is TEN SPACES on account 1 - confirmed byte by byte, all ten bytes 0x20. So :210 moves spaces, the keyed READ misses with FILE STATUS '23', :422 tolerates '00' OR '23' so nothing abends, and :437 moves 'DEFAULT' into an X(10) receiver making the retry key 'DEFAULT   '. This case seeds the WHOLE 51-row disclosure table rather than only the rows it reads, which strengthens the assertion: the miss is proved against the complete rate table INCLUDING the A000000000 block, so the fallback is not an artefact of having seeded only the DEFAULT rows, and the case simultaneously proves the program does not accidentally pick up the A-block. No row in the table carries a spaces group id, which is why the miss is genuine. THE TWO RATES, AND A SECOND CORRECTION DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY ADJUSTED. DIS-INT-RATE is read at 1-based 17-22 as '00150{' = 15.00 for both keys, because CVTRA02Y's DIS-GROUP-KEY is SIXTEEN bytes - X(10) + X(02) + 9(04) - and a 17-byte assumption would read the rate from 18-23 and corrupt every figure here. The brief's first sketch put row 2 on category 0004; the DEFAULT block's 01/0004 row actually carries '00250{' = 25.00, not 15.00, verified against the fixture. Rather than silently re-deriving row 2 at 25.00 or silently swapping the key, both facts are recorded: the verified 15.00 keys in the DEFAULT block are 01/0001, 04/0001, 04/0002, 04/0003, 05/0001, 06/0001 and 06/0002, and row 2 therefore uses type 04 category 0001. That keeps both rows under one account with two distinct 17-byte TRAN-CAT-KEYs and both at the same rate, which is what isolates the truncation difference to the balances. PER-FIELD RULINGS THE TWO WRITES ENCODE. TRAN-CAT-CD is 0005 on BOTH records and never 0001, 0004 or '05  ': :483 moves the alphanumeric literal '05' into a numeric-display PIC 9(04) receiver, which de-edits to the integer 5 and stores right-aligned and zero-filled. The input category drives the rate lookup ONLY and never reaches the output field - so the fact that the two records were computed from different categories is invisible in TRAN-CAT-CD by design, and an implementation that propagated 0001 and 0004 there would be wrong twice. Getting this span wrong shifts bytes 19-22 and cascades into all 331 that follow. TRAN-DESC is identical on both records: the literal 'Int. for a/c ' is thirteen characters including its trailing space, ACCT-ID is the ACCOUNT-RECORD field PIC 9(11) so it contributes 00000000001, the composed prefix is 24 bytes, and STRING does not blank the remainder of its receiver - bytes 57-132 are left exactly as the receiver found them. common.FixedWidthCodec builds the record with every PIC X span space-initialised, so that tail is 76 spaces, and because the prefix is invariably 24 bytes the tail is invariant across both writes rather than incidental to either. TRAN-TYPE-CD is 01 from :482. TRAN-SOURCE is 'System' plus FOUR trailing spaces, ten bytes. TRAN-MERCHANT-ID is nine zeros from MOVE 0 into PIC 9(09). The three merchant fields are 50, 50 and 10 spaces from :492-494. TRAN-CARD-NUM is 9680294154603697, resolved through the alternate index: :495 moves XREF-CARD-NUM, which :394-395 filled by READ XREF-FILE INTO CARD-XREF-RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-ACCT-ID over the XREFFIL1 path. The trailing FILLER PIC X(20) is never touched by 1300-B-WRITE-TX and is twenty spaces; it is pinned by name and the whole 350-byte image is pinned as well, which is two assertions rather than one - the named spans localise a failure, and the image proves the total width and therefore that the FILLER was emitted at all, since a record missing it is short by twenty bytes. 1400-COMPUTE-FEES IS INVOKED TWICE AND CONTRIBUTES NOTHING. :216 sits inside the satisfied IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0 guard at :214, so it runs once per row, but its body is the '* To be implemented' stub at :518-520 - a comment and an EXIT. No record, no field and no message either time. Implementing fee logic would be a new feature and a parity violation, so the twice-invoked no-op is asserted by the absence of any third write and by the exact row counts declared below. SEED PROVENANCE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. Four of the five inputs are unmodified fixture references named by row: ACCTFILE is acctdata.txt row 0, the only row whose ACCT-ID is 00000000001; XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 are both cardxref.txt row 48, the only row in that fixture whose XREF-ACCT-ID is 00000000001, found by matching bytes 26-36 rather than by assuming positional correspondence because the fixture is ordered by card number; and DISCGRP is the whole of discgrp.txt, all 51 rows. XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 carry deliberately identical bytes because app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:29-32 opens the base KSDS and an alternate-index PATH over that SAME cluster in one step - two access paths, not two datasets - and neither is mutated. Those cross-reference rows stay 36 bytes as seeded, because ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow owns the pad to CVACT03Y's declared 50 through the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below; the fixture itself is never edited, and the 50-byte form appears only in the final-state expectation, where the harness has already supplied the absent FILLER PIC X(14) as fourteen spaces. TCATBALF IS THE ONE INPUT THAT IS NOT VERBATIM FIXTURE DATA, AND IT CARRIES TWO SEPARATE OVERRIDES, BOTH DISCLOSED. First, the balances. Every one of tcatbal.txt's fifty rows carries TRAN-CAT-BAL '0000000000{', a zoned positive zero, so the raw fixture cannot exercise a truncating division at all. Second, the keys. Every one of those fifty rows uses type 01 and category 0001, so the raw fixture cannot place two different categories under one account either - which means the accumulation this case exists to prove is unreachable on it. Row 1 here is fixture row 0 - account 00000000001, type 01, category 0001, the genuine 17-byte TRAN-CAT-KEY - with its balance span and ONLY its balance span replaced, so the two images differ at exactly three bytes, all inside TRAN-CAT-BAL at 1-based 18-28, while the key at 1-11 / 12-13 / 14-17 and the FILLER X(22) at 29-50 are the fixture's own bytes untouched. Row 2 additionally changes the type and category to 04 and 0001, which is the override that makes two categories under one account possible; its FILLER is the same twenty-two fixture bytes. Neither balance is invented: 147.00 is account 3's real ACCT-CURR-BAL from acctdata.txt, '00000001470{' at 1-based 13-24, and 194.00 is account 1's own, '00000001940{' at the same offsets - the same digits one byte narrower here because ACCT-CURR-BAL is S9(10)V99 and TRAN-CAT-BAL is S9(09)V99. The rows are seeded in ascending key order, which matters because the DD is ORGANIZATION INDEXED with ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL at :28-32 and the account-break logic depends on the order records arrive in. Presenting a modified row as fixture data without saying so is the specific failure this disclosure exists to prevent. DETERMINISM, AND A THIRD DOCUMENTED DEVIATION. TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS are this program's only wall-clock values, both taking the same DB2-FORMAT-TS from Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP at :496-498, whose redefinition at :150-165 composes YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mm0000 to exactly 26 bytes. No 'now' is ever captured. Both records therefore carry the SAME timestamp, which the real program would also produce whenever two writes fall in the same hundredth of a second, and pinning removes the flakiness entirely rather than tolerating it. The case brief asked for these to be pinned at 2022-07-18-00.00.00.000000 and directed that the type be read and whatever it offers be used; the type offers pinnedClock on ScreenRequest ALONE, and ParityCase forbids a ScreenRequest on a BATCH_JOB outright, so a batch case cannot pin a clock of its own and 2022-07-18 is unreachable by construction. What applies instead is ParityHarness.DEFAULT_PINNED_CLOCK, which exists for exactly this reason and is fixed at 2022-07-19T23:12:34, rendering as the 26-byte 2022-07-19-23.12.34.000000. That instant is traceable rather than arbitrary: the repository-wide source footer reads 'Ver: CardDemo_v1.0-15-g27d6c6f-68 Date: 2022-07-19' and app/cbl/CBACT04C.cbl:651 stamps 2022-07-19 23:12:31 CDT. Bytes are US-ASCII throughout, matching the app/data/ASCII fixtures, never a platform default. A FOURTH DEVIATION, ON THE SHAPE OF THIS FILE ITSELF. The case brief asked for a member named expectedRecords. No such member exists on parity.ParityCase, which is the wire contract the brief itself names as authoritative and which the same brief requires this file to bind cleanly against. The two output channels the differ compares are expectedWrites - what the unit wrote, in write order - and expectedFinalState - what each seeded dataset holds afterwards - and they cannot be conflated because a dataset commonly appears on both with different counts. This case declares both, plus the unitKind that tells the harness how to invoke the unit, and the expectedDatasets row and width counts without which extra output would go unreported. Member order follows case01.json and case03.json exactly. WHAT IS COMPARED, AND HOW. The unit is reached at STEP level - account.AccountInterestCalcJob.calculateInterest with the declared parmDate and a captured SYSOUT sink - with no JobLauncher and no HTTP anywhere in the path, so the arithmetic is asserted directly. Nothing is compared as a whole string: each write pins all fourteen CVTRA05Y spans BY NAME in copybook order as well as the record image, and every difference the differ reports names a dataset, a row and a copybook field. Every dataset the case seeds is reported back on the final-state channel, not only the one the program can rewrite, so 'the inputs were not disturbed' is an assertion rather than an assumption - and here it covers all fifty-six seeded rows across five datasets, every one of them byte-identical to its seed. PROVENANCE OF THE EXPECTATIONS THEMSELVES. Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of the COBOL paragraphs, cross-checked against the CVTRA05Y, CVTRA01Y, CVTRA02Y, CVACT01Y and CVACT03Y byte layouts read offset by offset, the INTCALC.jcl DD and PARM contracts including :39 RECFM=F,LRECL=350, and the real ASCII fixtures. It was never captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment; that substitution is the plan's highest-severity open risk and is escalated rather than absorbed. No user rules were provided for this project - review_rules returns the single line 'No user rules provided.' and that is the whole document - so no rule mandates or forbids anything here, their absence is not treated as permission to lower the bar, and the plan's enterprise best-practice substitutes govern instead: B1 no placeholders, B3 reference inputs immutable, B4 all five departures from the brief above - the group id, the rate, the accumulation order, the clock and the shape of this file - documented rather than silently applied, B5 the dead code and the fee stub preserved, B7 the clock pinned, B8 scale 2 and RoundingMode.DOWN named explicitly and every dataset addressed through its binding key so no dataset name is written into source, B11 every offset read mechanically from the copybooks, and B12 both TCATBALF overrides and the derivation of every expectation disclosed.
